inbox.description: True while the pane has its message stream open, so a prompt goes through its queue.

oneOf.description: A runtime was added to the list, or its kind, colour or link state changed.
A runtime left the configuration and has no live link.

ClientRuntime.description: What a client needs of a runtime to mark its panes and offer it for a new pane.

Close.description: What the sweep does with a dead pane: keep stays, on_exit removes it after the linger grace.

Cwd.description:
Where a new pane starts: an absolute path of the host, or the directory of another pane. The
pane form needs a pane that the caller may read. The server maps the pane's directory into the
new pane's runtime, or to the host, through the runtimes' `paths`. When the pane's directory is
unknown or does not map, the new pane starts in the default directory.

Data.description: Any JSON value of at most 4096 bytes when encoded.

force.description:
Remove the live panes of the runtime first, as a stop does. Without force, live panes
refuse the request.

End.description: How a pane that has a parent ended.

ExecClient.description:
A message of the client of an exec session. The first one must be exec. The data of stdin is
at most 64 KiB before its encoding.

oneOf.description: Closes the input of the command.

ExecRequest.description:
Runs argv inside the runtime without a shell. The cwd is a path of the runtime. The env
applies after the env of the runtime. Without stdin the command reads an empty input.

ExecServer.description:
A message of the server in an exec session. After exit the server closes with 1000, and
after error with 1011. Error is the one way a session ends without exit.

oneOf.description: How the command ended: with an exit status, or by a signal.

ExitSignal.description: The signals by which a command can end. Other is any signal that this list does not name.

FrameNumber.description: 1 is the image itself; 2 and up are its animation frames.

Generation.description: The serial that the pane's terminal stamped on the frame.

ImageId.description: The id a program gave an image.

unshifted_codepoint.description: A Unicode scalar value: no surrogate, 0xD800 to 0xDFFF.

KillSignal.description: The signals that a client can send to the command of an exec session.

LeadReport.description: How the interactive step of a start ended, as the elected pane reports it.

stderr.description: The tail of the error output of the step. Its last line is the message of a failed start.

LinkState.description:
The state of a runtime's link. The first pane of a runtime starts it, and the idle rule or a
request takes it down.

inbox.description: True while the pane has its message stream open.

started.description: The pane's creation time in server monotonic nanoseconds.

Message.description:
A message on the message stream of a pane. The id is the sender's, so the receiver can drop a
repeat.

MessageId.description: The sender's id of a message: 8 to 64 characters of A-Z, a-z, 0-9, _ and -.

MessageState.description:
What a message is to the sender's knowledge: queued is in the pane's queue and not written,
delivered is written to the stream and not acked, acked is received.

Name.description: At most 256 bytes, without control characters.

Needle.description: The text to search for, percent-encoded in the query.

Offset.description: A byte offset of the pane's stream.

PathMap.description: A directory of the host and the directory of the runtime that holds the same files.

Posted.description:
The state of a sent message. The seq counts the messages of the pane in arrival order. A
repeat of an id that the pane has seen is a duplicate and gets the state of the original.

started.description: The server's monotonic start time in nanoseconds for a child record; absent on the root.

Relation.description: What the sender of a message is to its receiver, from the `parent` edges of the panes.

RuntimeInfo.description: What a client needs of a runtime to mark its panes and offer it for a new pane.

panes.description: The panes of the document that the runtime runs, dead ones included.

paths.description: The effective host-to-runtime prefix list that maps a host cwd.

socket.description: The path of the runtime's listener on the host, bound while the link is up.

RuntimeName.description: One to 32 bytes of a to z, 0 to 9 and -. host is not a runtime name.

RuntimePi.description: Where an agent's pi runs when it works in a runtime.

oneOf.description: On the host. Its built-in tools and `!` commands run in the runtime through exec sessions.
Inside the runtime, in a pane of the runtime.

RuntimeWait.description:
The reply of a wait on a runtime: its state when the wait ends. Only the one waiter that was
elected to run the interactive step gets lead, with the argv of that step.

SendKind.description: The kinds that a sender may give. The server reads none of them.

SendMessage.description: A message to the pane in the path. The server stamps the sender.

SendPrompt.description: A prompt for the agent in a pane. The scope is the window of `from`, else its session.

from.description: The pane that the prompt comes from. A pane identity may name only itself.

id.description: The id of the message when the prompt goes through the agent's message stream.

Sender.description:
The sender of a message, as the server knows it. The session and the name are those of a
pane that has a pi root.

ServerVersion.description: The reply of a running server: its version, and the instance that changes at each start.

SessionRef.description: A session id, or the name of a session.

wait_ms.description: Milliseconds to wait for the pane to end by itself before ko removes it.

StreamRequest.description:
What the receiver says about a message of its stream. A message that is neither acked nor
refused is written again to the next stream.

VarName.description: One to 256 bytes, without control characters.

runtimes.description: The configured runtimes in configuration order, with their link states.

info.description: The HTTP and WebSocket interface of the ko server on its unix socket.
info.title: ko server

get.description: The client-lifetime socket: layout, focus and status events.
The layout of every session, with its revision, and every pane that it names.

put.description: Replaces the layout. A stale revision gets 409 with the current layout.

get.description: Every pane, with its status and variables.

post.description: Creates a window with one pane, in one change of the layout. No client switches to it. The pane's session is the given one, else the parent's, else the caller's, else a new one. The window goes after the parent's or the caller's window of that session, else at the end.

get.description: One pane, with its status and variables.

post.description: Drops the scrollback of a pane.

get.description: One frame of an image of a pane. Frame 1 is the image itself. The reply is the pixels as an application/octet-stream body, with their format, size and timing in the ko-image-* headers. With the header Ko-Accept-Shm: 1 the reply is instead a JSON body that names a shared memory object, which the client maps and never unlinks. An image that was evicted, a frame that does not exist and a generation that moved on are not_found.

post.description: Sends a key, a mouse event, a paste or raw text to a pane.

get.description: The messages that other panes and the user send to a pane, one text message each, in the order of the pane's queue. The receiver answers each with an ack or a refuse. Only the pane itself may open the stream, and a pane has one stream at most.

post.description: Sends a message to a pane. The server stamps the sender and keeps the message in the pane's queue until the pane's stream gets it. A message that is written at once waits up to two seconds for its ack. An id that the pane has seen is not queued again: the reply is the state of the original, with duplicate set.

get.description: The text of a pane, from the server's terminal.

schema.description: none for the visible rows, all for the whole history, or the number of last rows.

get.description: A search of the pane's terminal, history included: the matches in batches, oldest first, then done. The rows count from the top of the history at the time of the search, for display only. Closing the socket cancels the search.

post.description: Waits up to wait_ms for the pane to end by itself, then removes it and hangs up its program. ko kills a removed program that still lives after the escalation time. A dead pane is removed at once.

delete.description: Removes variables of a pane, if its condition holds.
Removes one variable of a pane.

put.description: Sets one variable of a pane.

get.description: The view of a pane: the terminal byte stream, and the input of the viewer.

oneOf.description: The pane's terminal byte stream: one application/octet-stream message, framed as in docs/protocol.md section 4.

post.description: Sends a prompt to an agent.

get.description: The agents that a prompt can reach from the pane `from`. A pane identity may name only itself.
The runtimes of the configuration file and of the links that are up, with their state.

delete.description: Takes the runtime down, as down without force does, and removes its files except the empty io directory.

post.description: Takes the link of a runtime down. With live panes it is refused, unless force removes the panes first, as a stop does.

get.description: Runs one command inside a runtime, without a terminal: separate stdout and stderr, an exit status or signal, and stdin from the client. Each message is JSON text, and the first client message must be exec. The server reads the socket only while the command takes its stdin, and it sends output only while the connection's queue has room, so nothing is dropped. After exit the server closes with 1000, and after error with 1011. A runtime that is down starts as for a first pane. If its start needs a pane to log in, the session ends with an error. At most 32 sessions of one runtime run at once, and the others wait in order for KO_RUNTIME_EXEC_WAIT_MS. A closed socket stops the command. The route is for the host: a runtime connection is refused.

post.description: The pane that was elected to run the interactive step of a start reports how it ended.

get.description: Waits up to the timeout for the link of the runtime to be up or failed. Only a pane of the runtime may wait. The first waiter while the start has an interactive step gets that step's argv in lead, and an Up reply for a pane comes after the server wrote its token file.

delete.description: Closes every window of a session.

get.description: The protocol and terminal revisions of this server.

delete.description: Closes every pane of a window.
